title: VLM@school – Evaluation of AI image understanding on German middle school knowledge
extended_summary:
This paper presents VLM@school, a new benchmark for evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) on real German middle-school curriculum content. The authors argue that existing multimodal benchmarks often rely on English-language, multiple-choice, or decontextualized tasks that do not adequately reflect practical visual reasoning demands. To address this, they construct a dataset of 486 images and 2,038 open-ended questions drawn from grades 8–10 across nine school subjects, including mathematics, biology, geography, history, music, religion, arts, physics, and sports.

The benchmark is not an educational intervention with students, but an evaluation framework for AI models. Questions were created by native German speakers, often tied to images from textbooks and other instructional materials, and some items were deliberately adversarial to test whether models can refuse to answer when the image does not support the question. The authors evaluate 13 open-weight VLMs using LLM-as-a-judge with multiple judges to score open-ended responses.

Results show that even strong current models perform poorly on these middle-school tasks, with the best overall score below 45% and especially weak performance in math, music, and adversarial questions. The paper concludes that middle-school-level multimodal questions are a useful stress test for VLMs, that German-language and open-ended evaluation exposes substantial limitations not seen on common benchmarks, and that future work should compare German with English versions and explore reasoning-based prompting.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed benchmark/evaluation study with a clear methodology, but it is not an intervention study and does not include experimental assignment or causal identification. It mainly provides descriptive performance evidence from model benchmarking rather than high-credibility outcome evaluation in schools.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has useful adjacent evidence for likely AI performance on middle-school-style math and multimodal tasks, but it does not estimate student learning gains or implementation effects. Its practical implication is mostly diagnostic: current open-weight VLMs show limited accuracy and weak refusal behavior on middle-school-level questions.

interventions.use_case: Benchmarking and evaluating vision-language models on German middle school curriculum questions that require visual reasoning plus subject knowledge; includes open-ended QA and adversarial unanswerable questions rather than tutoring or instruction.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that the best overall VLM achieved only about 34.09% accuracy on the math domain, with the strongest overall model reaching 34.09% and the weakest 9.09% on math questions (n=308 math questions). The authors note that models were better at calculating than at counting, and that errors in reading shapes or coordinates often propagated into incorrect answers.
finding.measure: Accuracy on open-ended middle school math questions involving geometry, counting, area, circumference, and coordinate reading

finding.finding_summary: Across the full benchmark, the best model reached 43.26% overall accuracy and all models remained below 45%, indicating substantial difficulty on middle-school level multimodal subject questions. Domain performance was especially weak in music (best 31.03%), while history and religion were comparatively higher (best around 54%), showing strong domain variation rather than robust mastery.
finding.measure: Overall and domain-specific accuracy on open-ended multimodal middle school subject questions

finding.finding_summary: The benchmark includes adversarial questions designed to test whether models can say 'I don't know' when the answer is not visible in the image. Performance was very low overall, with the best model reaching only 32.83% on adversarial questions and many models scoring around 10%-15%, indicating poor uncertainty recognition and weak resistance to misleading prompts.
finding.measure: Accuracy on adversarial/unanswerable questions requiring rejection of misleading image-linked premises
finding.study_size: subset of the n=2038 questions; adversarial counts not fully reported
